title: Deep link routing for iPad
description: Update DeepLinkRouter in AggregatorApp/AggregatorApp.swift to detect the active navigation model. On iPad (hSizeClass == .regular or by reading @Environment iPadNavigationModel): aggregator://thread/{id} sets iPadNavigationModel.selectedSection = .threads and selectedThread to the thread with the given id; aggregator://article/{id} sets selectedSection and selectedArticle. On iPhone: existing selectedTab logic must remain completely unchanged. iPadNavigationModel must already be in the environment (from the NavigationModel bead).
acceptance_criteria: DeepLinkRouter dispatches to iPadNavigationModel on iPad
aggregator://thread/{id} navigates to correct thread on iPad
aggregator://article/{id} navigates to correct article on iPad
iPhone deep link behavior is unchanged
Malformed deep links do not crash the app

handoff_summary.completed: DeepLinkRouter.handle() extended with iPadNavModel parameter that sets selectedSection (.threads for thread links, .today for article links). AggregatorApp.onOpenURL passes iPadNavModel. AppRootIPad adds @Environment(DeepLinkRouter.self), @State capturedDeepLink, consumePendingLink(), detailContent overlay that shows ThreadDetailView/ArticleDetailView via deep link, and onChange handlers to clear capturedDeepLink when user selects items normally.
handoff_summary.risks: Article deep links set selectedSection to .today, which switches the content column to TodayIPadView. This may be slightly confusing since the today section shows daily briefs rather than individual articles — a future iteration could introduce a dedicated articles section or route to .search instead.
handoff_summary.next_action: Hand off to tester agent to verify deep link routing on iPad simulator: aggregator://thread/{id} switches to threads section and shows ThreadDetailView; aggregator://article/{id} switches to today section and shows ArticleDetailView; malformed URLs are silently ignored; iPhone tab switching is unaffected.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: AppRootIPad.swift was already modified by bead B-80cd72ae (section wiring). This bead's changes are additive: new properties, new computed view, new lifecycle modifiers. No overlapping edits.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: 1. DeepLinkRouter.handle() accepts iPadNavigationModel as an optional parameter (default nil) rather than storing a persistent reference. This keeps the router stateless with respect to the iPad model and avoids retain-cycle risk. The caller (AggregatorApp.onOpenURL) passes it explicitly. 2. AppRootIPad captures router.pendingLink into local @State (capturedDeepLink) and clears router.pendingLink immediately. This prevents ThreadsView on iPhone from racing with the iPad handler, and gives the detail column a stable, non-reactive binding. 3. User-initiated selections (selectedThread, selectedArticle, etc.) clear capturedDeepLink via onChange so the section-based sectionDetailContent resumes naturally. 4. Article deep links route to .today section (closest to an articles context in the iPad sidebar). Thread deep links route to .threads. 5. Both deep-link detail views are wrapped in NavigationStack to support any in-detail navigation (e.g., external links inside ArticleDetailView). .id(id) ensures SwiftUI recreates the stack if the same link type fires twice with a different ID.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: Tester should verify: (1) aggregator://thread/123 on iPad simulator switches sidebar to Threads and renders ThreadDetailView in the detail column; (2) aggregator://article/456 on iPad switches to Today section and renders ArticleDetailView; (3) tapping a thread in ThreadsIPadView after a deep link arrival dismisses the deep-link detail and shows the tapped thread; (4) aggregator://unknown/1 and aggregator://thread/abc (non-integer) are silently ignored; (5) on iPhone simulator, existing tab-switching and ThreadsView navigation still works for both thread and article deep links.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: 1. Article deep links switch the content column to TodayIPadView (daily briefs list), which is contextually mismatched — the detail shows an article but the content pane shows briefs. A future bead should introduce a dedicated articles section or reroute article links to .search. 2. capturedDeepLink is cleared whenever any selection property changes, including selections in unrelated sections (e.g., selecting a podcast episode clears a pending thread deep link). This is conservative and correct but could be narrowed.

conflict_risks: AppRootIPad.swift was already modified by bead B-80cd72ae (section wiring). This bead's changes are additive: new properties, new computed view, new lifecycle modifiers. No overlapping edits.

execution_history.summary: Implemented deep link routing for iPad. DeepLinkRouter.handle() now accepts an optional iPadNavigationModel and sets selectedSection when a URL is handled. AppRootIPad captures router.pendingLink into local state, clears it, and renders ThreadDetailView or ArticleDetailView in the detail column. User-initiated selection changes clear the captured deep link so the section-based detail view resumes. iPhone behavior is unchanged. Build passes.

# Developer Guardrails

Primary responsibility: Implement only the assigned bead inside the existing architecture and file scope.

## Corrective bead scope

If your `bead_id` ends in `-corrective` or `-corrective-<N>` (e.g. `B-abc12345-corrective`, `B-abc12345-test-corrective-2`), you are running as a CORRECTIVE bead. Your scope is **strictly limited to fixing the specific failure that blocked the parent bead**. Do not:

- Add unrelated improvements, refactors, or cleanup, even if you notice them
- Reapply previously-reverted changes (the operator reverted them for a reason)
- Expand the surface area beyond what is needed to unblock the parent
- Touch files outside what the parent bead's `expected_files` / `expected_globs` covered, unless the failure is genuinely in another file and there is no smaller fix

If you notice an unrelated issue while fixing the corrective scope: **file a separate bead** via `takt bead create` describing what you saw, but do not fix it in this corrective. The operator will prioritize and dispatch.

When in doubt about scope: prefer the smallest possible fix. The reviewer of this corrective will check that the scope was respected.

Allowed actions:
- Modify code, configuration, or local docs required to complete the assigned bead.
- Create sub-beads for discovered follow-up work that should be handled separately.
- Verify your `Swift` changes compile and import correctly with a quick syntax check: ``.

Disallowed actions:
- Run any test suite — not even a targeted `` run or any subset. Test execution is exclusively the tester agent's responsibility. Running tests wastes the agent budget and delays the pipeline.
- Redesign unrelated architecture or broaden scope beyond the assigned bead.
- Perform final review signoff in place of a review agent.
- Silently absorb unrelated test, documentation, or planning work that should be handed off.

## Memory

**Read memory at bead start.** Before touching any code, run three searches using `$TAKT_CMD` (injected by the orchestrator):

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace global
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace specs
```

Treat results as ambient context — apply relevant entries; skip entries that don't apply.

**Write to memory when you discover reusable project knowledge** — something that would have changed your approach if you had known it upfront, and is not already in CLAUDE.md or the guardrails.

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<concise fact>" --namespace global               # project-wide knowledge
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<discovery>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>  # feature-scoped
```

Required Handoff Fields:

Every developer bead **must** populate the following three fields in its output JSON. Reviewers and tester agents rely on these fields to scope their work without additional back-and-forth turns. Use `"N/A"` only when a field is genuinely inapplicable (e.g., a trivial rename with no design trade-offs); do not leave fields blank.

- **`design_decisions`** — Document non-obvious architectural or implementation choices made during this bead. Include alternatives considered and why the chosen approach was preferred. Reviewers use this to evaluate correctness without re-deriving intent. Set to `"N/A"` only if the change was purely mechanical with no meaningful trade-offs.

- **`test_coverage_notes`** — Describe what the tester agent should verify: new code paths, edge cases introduced, regression risks, and any known untested scenarios left to the tester. Set to `"N/A"` only if the bead touched no executable code paths (e.g., documentation-only changes).

- **`known_limitations`** — Call out constraints, deferred work, or known gaps in the implementation. This includes out-of-scope items deliberately left for follow-up beads and any areas where the implementation is intentionally incomplete. Set to `"N/A"` if the implementation is complete as specified with no known gaps.

Expected outputs:
- Completed or blocked JSON with concise implementation summary.
- Accurate touched files, changed files, risks, and follow-up handoff fields.
- Populated `design_decisions`, `test_coverage_notes`, and `known_limitations` fields in every response.
